The circular has been issued with the approval of the competent authority.
Article Summary: Every medical college regulated by the National Medical Commission will now have to set up an "Enabling Unit" The move follows the NMC's new guidelines on assessing students with benchmark disabilities for MBBS admissions. According to the circular, the Enabling Unit will function as the single point of contact for students with benchmarks disabilities.

Article Title: Ex-top Chhattisgarh official behind paper leaks, appointed kin as deputy collector, DSP: ED
Article Text:
Representative image

ED has taken custodial remand of Taman Singh Sonwani, a retired IAS who served as chairperson of Chhattisgarh Public Service Commission (CGPSC), in an alleged case of paper leak and manipulation of CGPSC state service exam.Sonwani in 2021 allegedly amended recruitment rules of CGPSC to remove "nephew" from the definition of "family" and appointed his family members as deputy collector and DSP, according to ED.A special court in Raipur has remanded him to ED custody for seven days, till July 30 for further investigation. The former IAS officer was arrested on July 25.
Article Summary: Taman Singh Sonwani was chairperson of Chhattisgarh Public Service Commission. He allegedly amended recruitment rules of CGPSC to remove "nephew" from definition of "family" and appointed his family members as deputy collector and DSP. He was arrested on July 25.

Article Title: Ayodhya Ram mandir donation row: On Supreme Court suggestion, temple SIT to include a forensic auditor
Article Text:
During the last hearing, the bench had warned petitioners against politicising the issue

NEW DELHI: The UP government on Monday immediately accepted Supreme Court's suggestion for inclusion of a chartered accountant having expertise in forensic audit in the three-member SIT, constituted on the Supreme Court's July 20 order to investigate alleged embezzlement of donations to Ayodhya Ram mandir managed by Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust.As soon as a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana sought to know the UP govt's view on inclusion of a chartered accountant having expertise in forensic audit in the SIT headed by IGP Kiran S, solicitor general Tushar Mehta said, "Without taking instructions from the govt, I am assuring the court that such an expert will be drafted into the SIT."The bench said, "We want an expeditious, fair and transparent investigation into all aspects of allegations relating to alleged misappropriation of donation funds for the temple managed by the trust."Appearing for a PIL petitioner, advocate Devadatt Kamat said since there were allegations of siphoning out of donations meant for temple construction from across the country, the trust should be asked to upload all receipts of donations on its website."This will help devotees identify whether their donations for construction of the temple and thereafter have been accounted for or not," Kamat said and requested the court to entrust supervision of the SIT probe to a retired Supreme Court judge.The SG objected and said, "We must trust the Supreme Court and three honourable judges who are monitoring it."The CJI-led bench turned down Kamat's request and said, "When we are monitoring the probe being carried out by the SIT, there is no need of any supervision by a retired judge. The SIT will transparently investigate all aspects of allegations relating to siphoning of funds." It asked the SIT to submit a probe status report in two weeks.During the last hearing, the bench had warned petitioners against politicising the issue and assured that there would be fair, impartial, transparent and expeditious investigation by the SIT. Supreme Court said if the SIT experienced any impediment from any quarter in carrying out the investigation, it should approach Supreme Court without loss of time.
Article Summary: The UP government on Monday immediately accepted Supreme Court's suggestion for inclusion of a chartered accountant having expertise in forensic audit in the three-member SIT. The SIT is constituted on the Supreme court's July 20 order to investigate alleged embezzlement of donations to Ayodhya Ram mandir managed by Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust.

Article Title: Coast Guard airlifts ailing seafarer from ship off Gujarat coast despite rough seas, adverse weather
Article Text:
Seafarer was airlifted to safety off the Gujarat coast

NEW DELHI: A seafarer was airlifted to safety off the Gujarat coast after the Indian Coast Guard carried out a difficult medical evacuation despite rough seas and adverse weather.In a post on X, Indian Coast Guard said that it “successfully executed a MEDEVAC of a 21-year-old seafarer from MT Murlikisan off Porbandar on 26 July 2026. With a swift response from MRCC Mumbai, CGDHQ-1 Porbandar swung into action, providing immediate telemedical assistance while deploying surface and air assets. The patient was airlifted using an ICG Advanced Light Helicopter to Porbandar, medically stabilised by ICG doctors, and shifted to Hospital for further treatment.”The seafarer was reported to be suffering from acute chest pain and a high fever, requiring urgent medical attention.The helicopter successfully winched the patient from the vessel and transported him to the Coast Guard Air Enclave, where an Indian Coast Guard medical officer provided initial stabilisation. Officials said the successful evacuation underscores “ICG's steadfast dedication to maritime safety and reflects the spirit of Vayam Rakshamah (We Protect).”A few days ago, the Coast Guard evacuated a 29-year-old Indian mariner suffering from a medical emergency aboard the tanker 'MT Kashimasan' off the Goa coast, transferring him ashore for urgent treatment.
Article Summary: A seafarer was airlifted to safety off the Gujarat coast after the Indian Coast Guard carried out a difficult medical evacuation. The 21-year-old was reported to be suffering from acute chest pain and a high fever, requiring urgent medical attention.

Article Title: Jammu and Kashmir: Mehbooba faces heat over Jantar Mantar comment, opposition accuses her justifying use of force in UT
Article Text:
File photo: People's Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti

SRINAGAR: PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti ’s comment at the Jantar Mantar protest, where she appeared to justify the use of force in Kashmir by citing “militancy”, has invited a backlash in J&K, with governing NC and other parties demanding her apology.Leading the NC charge, chief minister Omar Abdullah said Mehbooba stayed away from his party’s July 20 protest at Jantar Mantar to press for restoration of statehood, but defended the suppression of Kashmiris in the guise of fighting “militancy” at the same venue. If a crackdown on people seeking their rights is supported by people in positions of power, it would deter Kashmiris from protesting for statehood or any other cause, he argued. The PDP chief should admit that she got carried away and should say sorry, Omar said.A defensive PDP claimed her remark had been twisted, but this drew further criticism.Mehbooba visited Jantar Mantar on July 23 to extend support to the CJP-led protest over the NEET paper leak. Referring to the use of force against protesters in Delhi, she drew a parallel with Kashmir.“We have seen this for the first time in Delhi. We have witnessed it in Kashmir for many years.Magar wahan militancy hai, uska ek banta hai (But militancy exists there, so it is understandable). There, you have militants on one side and security forces on the other. Here, no one is a militant and they (protesters) don’t even have stones in their hands,” she is heard saying in a widely circulated video.It’s the “banta hai” remark that has kicked up a storm. “She appeared to justify the misuse of power in Jammu and Kashmir , arrests and other actions, by saying that due to militancy here, such measures are acceptable. In what sense are they acceptable? Does militancy mean the law should not be followed? Does it mean our children should not get justice? Does it mean people’s passports should be withheld?” the CM asked.“This old habit of saying one thing in Jammu and Kashmir and another in Delhi has still not gone away,” he added.“A former chief minister has stated it is acceptable to suppress people’s protests through force. After such a statement, no Kashmiri will feel encouraged to come out and fight for their rights,” Omar further said.PDP legislator Waheed Para claimed Mehbooba’s comment had been misrepresented. According to him, she was only making the point that while the repression in Kashmir was carried out in the name of fighting terrorism and “militancy,” what justification did the authorities have for using force against protesters in Delhi.PC staged a protest against Mehbooba’s remark. “During her tenure, bloodshed took place, pellet guns were used and thousands of our youths suffered. Those who suffered cannot now be branded as militants,” the party said.
Article Summary: Mehbooba Mufti appeared to justify the use of force in Kashmir by citing “militancy’ Her comment invited a backlash in J&K, with governing NC and other parties demanding her apology. A defensive PDP claimed her remark had been twisted, but this drew further criticism.

Article Title: 'No legal action, FIRs being withdrawn': Bihar govt assures protesters in big win for students, CJP
Article Text:
Protesters damage a police vehicle during the 'Bihar Bandh' called over the alleged NEET paper leak and police action against protesting students, in Patna, Bihar. (PTI photo)

Cockroach Janta Party warns of fresh protests

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: The Bihar government on Monday announced the withdrawal of FIRs against all protesters who were arrested for alleged involvement in last week's violent protests over the NEET (UG) issue in the state.According to the Bihar government's home department, the relief would apply to all cases registered up to 6 pm on July 26, a day after the demonstrations.The home department further stated that those arrested within this period would be released and no further action would be taken against any of the accused.The announcement came hours after the Bihar Police, while detailing the violence during the demonstrations, stated that 694 people — nearly half of them minors — were detained for allegedly attempting to enforce a state-wide bandh last week over the NEET paper leak issue.According to the statement, violence during the July 25 bandh, called by Left-wing students' unions, left 91 personnel and officials, two administrative officers and 13 civilians injured.Among those detained, "339 minors and students" were released after age verification, while the remaining 355 were produced before courts and were facing proceedings "for involvement in violent activities."Thirteen government vehicles were vandalised and another was set on fire by bandh supporters.Those injured in the incidents included the SP of Siwan and SDPOs from Siwan and Sitamarhi districts.In Saran, two Block Development Officers (BDOs) suffered grievous injuries, with one losing an eye and the other sustaining a serious head injury.Both BDOs were "battling for life" at separate hospitals in Patna, the state capital.Meanwhile, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), the youth outfit that led protests in Delhi over the NEET (UG) paper leak issue, on Monday warned the Centre of renewed demonstrations if cases against protesters across the country were not withdrawn.The withdrawal of cases was one of the CJP's three conditions for calling off its agitation, which it ended on July 25 after the Centre accepted all its demands.The CJP had been holding an indefinite protest since June 21, seeking accountability over the paper leak issue. On July 20, a march to Parliament organised by the outfit turned violent, leaving protesters and security personnel injured.
Article Summary: Bihar government announces withdrawal of FIRs against all protesters arrested for alleged involvement in last week's violent protests. The relief would apply to all cases registered up to 6 pm on July 26, a day after the demonstrations. The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), the youth outfit that led protests in Delhi over the NEET (UG) paper leak issue, on Monday warned the Centre of renewed demonstrations.

Article Title: 47 GW battery storage, 23 GW pumped storage projects in pipeline
Article Text:
Representative AI-generated image

NEW DELHI: India has nearly 47 GW of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity at various stages of development as the country ramps up storage infrastructure to support rapid expansion of renewable energy and meet rising electricity demand, power ministry informed Parliament Monday.As of June 30, nearly 16 GW of BESS capacity was under construction, about 12 GW awarded, while another 19 GW is at the tendering stage, MoS for power Shripad Yesso Naik said in a written reply in Rajya Sabha. On the pumped storage front, 16 GW of projects are under construction, while another 7 GW has received concurrence and is awaiting construction.As per National Electricity Plan (Generation), India is projected to require 47 GW of battery energy storage capacity and 27 GW of pumped storage capacity by 2031-32. The minister said large-scale deployment of storage systems will be critical for integrating renewable energy, meeting peak electricity demand and ensuring grid reliability.The minister also said India will require investments of about Rs 4.8 lakh crore in energy storage infrastructure by 2031-32 to support the growing share of renewable energy in the power mix. Of the total investment, about Rs 3.5 lakh crore is estimated for battery energy storage systems and Rs 1.3 lakh crore for pumped storage projects.The storage push comes alongside an aggressive capacity addition programme. Since April 2023, 21 GW of thermal power capacity has been commissioned, while 48 GW, including 4.8 GW of stressed projects, is under construction. Contracts have also been awarded for another 16 GW of coal- and lignite-based capacity.On the renewable side, 148 GW of capacity is under construction, while another 48 GW is at various stages of planning and targeted for completion by 2029-30.The ministry said India’s installed power generation capacity is projected to reach 874 GW by 2031-32, with states preparing 10-year resource adequacy plans to ensure generation capacity remains ahead of projected demand.
Article Summary: India has nearly 47 GW of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity at various stages of development. The country is ramping up storage infrastructure to support rapid expansion of renewable energy. As of June 30, nearly 16 GW of BESS capacity was under construction, about 12 GW awarded, while another 19 GW is at the tendering stage.

Article Title: NHAI wins major arbitration, Rs 3,177-cr claim cut to Rs 46 cr
Article Text:
The NHAI’s wins major arbitration case

NEW DELHI: NHAI, in a recent arbitration case, has got an arbitration order in its favour, rejecting the majority of claims – against the claim of Rs 3,177 crore by a contractor; the arbitral tribunal awarded only Rs 46 crore to settle the case.In an official statement, the highways authority said that the arbitration case involved 151-km Bareilly-Sitapur BOT (Toll) highway project in Uttar Pradesh.The dispute arose after NHAI terminated the concession agreement with Bareilly Highways Project Limited (BHPL), a company promoted by Era Infra Engineering Ltd, in May 2019. The concessionaire had sought compensation of around Rs 3,177 crore through 30 claims before a three-member arbitral tribunal.In its award, the tribunal allowed only three claims worth about Rs 46 crore, along with applicable interest, while rejecting the overwhelming majority of the claims. The tribunal also upheld the validity of the “supplementary agreement” signed on March 30, 2015, and ruled that delays in the project were concurrent, weakening the concessionaire's case.NHAI had filed counterclaims relating to financial losses and public inconvenience caused by the stalled project.Although these counterclaims were not accepted, the authority successfully defended itself against the bulk of the concessionaire's claims, substantially reducing its potential financial exposure.The latest ruling adds to a series of arbitration successes for NHAI this year. In June, it secured an award of Rs 1,202 crore in the Tumkur-Chitradurga six-laning project in Karnataka. Earlier, arbitration in the Panipat-Jalandhar highway project involving claims exceeding Rs 8,000 crore was settled at Rs 819.96 crore in NHAI's favour. In another case relating to the Kamrej-Chalthan section of NH-48 in Gujarat, claims of Rs 174.5 crore were reduced to just Rs 54 lakh.toied
Article Summary: The dispute arose after NHAI terminated the concession agreement with Bareilly Highways Project Limited (BHPL), a company promoted by Era Infra Engineering Ltd. The concessionaire had sought compensation of around Rs 3,177 crore through 30 claims before a three-member arbitral tribunal. The tribunal allowed only three claims worth about Rs 46 crore, along with applicable interest.

Article Title: 'Will support any decision taken in discharge of duty': CRPF leadership assures personnel
Article Text:
Representational image

NEW DELHI: The Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) has assured its personnel that any decision taken in the "bona fide discharge of their duties" in the recent past would have the full backing of the force's top leadership, officials said on Monday."The CRPF headquarters has lauded the endurance and patience exhibited by the personnel while discharging their duties during the difficult situation they faced recently," officials told PTI."The top brass underlined and stressed that any decision made by the troops and ground officers in the interest of the nation, the force and for the bona fide discharge of their duties will have the headquarters' support," they added.The message came on the CRPF's 87th Raising Day. A communication in this regard was sent to the field formations of the country's largest paramilitary force, which handles various internal security duties, including riot and crowd control.Although the message did not specify what it meant by the "recent past", it came days after the Rapid Action Force (RAF), the CRPF's specialised riot-control wing, allegedly used pellet guns against student protesters during their march to Parliament in Delhi on July 20.The force is probing the alleged use of pellet guns by the RAF.On this, officials asserted that any "reckless or unjustified action" by RAF personnel would invite disciplinary action as per the CRPF's rules and applicable law.They reiterated that a formal Court of Inquiry (CoI) would be initiated once the RAF/CRPF probe establishes that the troops' actions in Delhi last week were unjustified or violated standard operating procedures (SOPs).The probe is examining around 9-10 allegations against RAF/CRPF personnel, based on multiple social media videos and press reports, as well as instances where some jawans were allegedly left stranded and attacked by miscreants.According to officials, the inquiry is looking into the circumstances under which pellet guns and shock batons were reportedly used. They said the choice of weapon rests with the jawan on the ground, but any such decision must be justified and based on valid reasoning.
Article Summary: The Central Reserve Police Force assured its personnel that any decision taken in the "bona fide discharge of their duties" in the recent past would have the full backing of the force's top leadership. A communication in this regard was sent to the field formations of the country's largest paramilitary force. It came days after the Rapid Action Force (RAF), the CRPF's specialised riot- control wing, allegedly used pellet guns against student protesters in Delhi.

Article Title: 'Different flags, same playbook': Sonam Wangchuk's wife slams BJP, Congress
Article Text:
Gitanjali J Angmo, wife of educator and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk, calls out both BJP and Congress in a post on X

NEW DELHI: Gitanjali J Angmo, wife of activist Sonam Wangchuk , on Monday criticised both the BJP and the Congress , saying political rivals used the same playbook to label those who disagreed with them."When Wangchuk was detained, the BJP IT cell called us anti-national, Chinese agents, foreign-funded, and every other label they could manufacture. Today, because we called the Congress' protest at PM's residence insincere, Congress trolls are calling us Sanghis, RSS and BJP stooges," Angmo said in a post on X."Different flags. Same playbook. The rot has infected our entire political culture."She added that India needed more than just a change of government. "It needs a change in the very grammar of politics, where disagreement is met with dialogue, not demonisation; where patriotism is measured by integrity, not party affiliation; and where truth matters more than tribal loyalty."Angmo had previously criticised the flash protest led by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi outside PM Modi's residence on July 21, calling it "insincere.""The protest outside the PM's house lacked sincerity. It would have been more sincere if it had been done by joining hands at Jantar Mantar. So, the public cannot be fooled anymore. This is an awakened India," Angmo said in an interview.
Article Summary: Gitanjali J Angmo, wife of activist Sonam Wangchuk, criticises both BJP and Congress. She says political rivals used the same playbook to label those who disagreed with them. Angmo had previously criticised the flash protest led by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi outside PM Modi's residence.

Article Title: Bihar's dairy push: New plant in Nalanda to boost farmer incomes, create jobs
Article Text:
Bihar bets big on value-added dairy, launches 20 MTPD curd and lassi plant in Nalanda

COMFED outlines expansion roadmap

Bihar laid the foundation stone for a modern 20 metric tonne per day curd and lassi processing plant in Nalanda, on Monday. This marks a significant step in the state's ambition to emerge as a stronger player in India's fast-growing dairy industry.Chief minister Samrat Choudhary laid the foundation for the facility at the Biharsharif Dairy Project, which is expected to substantially enhance the production capacity of COMFED's flagship brand Sudha. The expansion aims to meet rising demand for value-added dairy products while preparing the brand to compete in global markets as India strengthens its position as the world's largest milk producer.The new facility is expected to encourage further investments in dairy processing, reinforce Bihar's efforts to build a robust dairy value chain, and deliver higher returns to farmers. It also positions the state to capitalise on India's growing competitive advantage in the global dairy sector.The expansion is closely aligned with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of 'Sahkar Se Samriddhi' (Prosperity through Cooperation) and the objectives of White Revolution 2.0, launched by Union home and cooperation minister Amit Shah. As India seeks to strengthen its dairy cooperative movement and enhance the global footprint of Indian dairy products, Sudha is steadily evolving from a trusted regional brand into a nationally respected and globally competitive dairy brand.Towards this objective, COMFED is expanding village-level dairy cooperative societies, increasing milk procurement, and promoting greater participation of women in the dairy economy.Addressing the gathering, chief minister Choudhary commended COMFED and Bihar's dairy cooperatives for their contribution to the state's rural economy and expressed confidence that Sudha would evolve into a globally competitive dairy brand. "Sudha represents much more than a dairy brand. It is the backbone of the livelihoods, self-reliance and aspirations of millions of dairy farmers across Bihar," he said.Through its extensive cooperative network, Sudha has ensured that producers receive fair remuneration while strengthening the rural economy and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities.Shirsat Kapil Ashok, Managing Director of COMFED, highlighted the federation's achievements during the first 100 days of the present government, including the formation of more than 2,500 new dairy cooperative societies across Bihar. This has resulted in an increase of over 300,000 litres of milk procurement per day compared to the previous year.Outlining the roadmap for the next 100 days, Ashok said COMFED would expand initiatives such as Sudha Sakhi and the Prime Minister's Veterinary Medicine Centres, while implementing key livestock breed improvement projects. These include a proposed Semen Station in Lakhisarai and an AITI Centre in Munger, aimed at improving cattle genetics and productivity.The chief minister distributed deep freezers to 300 retailers to strengthen Sudha's frozen products distribution network and flagged off a specially designed vehicle for transporting sick and infirm livestock.
Article Summary: Bihar laid the foundation stone for a modern 20 metric tonne per day curd and lassi processing plant in Nalanda. This marks a significant step in the state's ambition to emerge as a stronger player in India's fast-growing dairy industry. The expansion aims to meet rising demand for value-added dairy products.

Article Title: 'Modi govt fears truth and non-violence': Rahul Gandhi on Ken-Betwa protest crackdown
Article Text:
Police cleared the protest site on July 19

Rahul Gandhi X post

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Monday said the Narendra Modi government fears "both truth and non-violent resistance", days after police dispersed tribal protests against the Ken-Betwa river linking project in BJP-led Madhya Pradesh."The tribal brothers and sisters of Madhya Pradesh had sat on a water satyagraha and hunger strike because their land was taken away for the Ken-Betwa project, but they received neither fair compensation nor dignified rehabilitation," the Lok Sabha leader of opposition wrote on X.Calling tribals the country's "original owners", Rahul Gandhi asserted that the first right over water, forests and land "belongs to them alone.""And their 'satyagraha' is because that very right is being snatched from them today. In their unique way, their demand is simply this: provide a proper means of livelihood—or else life is no different from a funeral pyre. But even this is unacceptable to the BJP government. Instead of listening to them, their peaceful protest is being crushed with police force," the Raebareli MP added.The former Congress chief expressed solidarity with the protesting tribal communities and asserted that his party would ensure justice, including fair compensation and proper rehabilitation for them.Rahul Gandhi also shared a video clip highlighting the protests in Madhya Pradesh.On July 19, police in Madhya Pradesh's Chhatarpur district removed protesters from the site, bringing their 15-day agitation to an end.The Rs 44,605-crore Ken-Betwa Link Project is India's first river-linking project under the National Perspective Plan. It aims to irrigate 1.062 million hectares of land, provide drinking water to around 6.2 million people, and generate hydropower in the drought-prone Bundelkhand region spanning Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi: Narendra Modi government fears "both truth and non-violent resistance" Police dispersed tribal protests against the Ken-Betwa river linking project in Madhya Pradesh. The Rs 44,605-crore project is India's first river- linking project under the National Perspective Plan.
